analysis.title: Lighthouse Goes Dark: After Jupiter, Oracle's 1.3GW Wisconsin Data Center Is Next To Face Major Delays
key_insights: Aterio reports a meaningful risk that power for Oracle's 1.3GW Project Lighthouse campus (Port Washington, WI, developed by Vantage, part of OpenAI's Stargate) arrives after Oracle's guidance of customer delivery in 2H27. The campus cannot run until American Transmission Co. (ATC) connects it, and ATC cannot build until the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin (PSC) approves.

The PSC unanimously revoked its completeness finding on ATC's application on August 7, reportedly the first time in recent decades, after ATC filed or refiled 564 documents following the December 2025 completeness determination. The PSC closed the case September 10 without ruling on the merits, and ATC refiled September 18, restarting the statutory clock.

Wisconsin law gives the PSC 30 days to rule on completeness (next deadline October 19), then 180 days to decide, extendable once by 180 days, plus 6 months' notice before construction. Aterio says construction cannot start before March 2027. Partial power (about 310MW) comes about 7 months after construction starts and full power about 17 months after.

Aterio scenarios: early (unlikely) partial power October 2027 and full 1.3GW August 2028. Base case partial power December 2027 and full October 2028. Extended review partial power June 2028 and full April 2029. The PSC extended its review in every comparable large transmission case, with 345kV decisions taking 355-358 days from completeness.

ATC's Ozaukee County Distribution Interconnection Project is now estimated at $2.48-2.72B, up from $1.3-1.7B in the original application. About $1.1B is the Decker grid-stabilization system (E-STATCOM), which Oracle agreed to fund.

The article argues the extended scenario is realistic, putting full power in spring 2029. This makes two of Oracle's five major campuses (New Mexico's Project Jupiter and Wisconsin) flagged as late, two weeks after Barclays said there was no read-through to other sites.

Wisconsin is the only Oracle campus relying entirely on a utility grid build-out. The Texas sites use ERCOT plus on-site gas or behind-the-meter gas, and New Mexico was planned as a behind-the-meter fuel cell microgrid.
Barclays says Saline, Michigan has already secured power and permits and is one of the most de-risked assets in Oracle's pipeline. First delivery there is due by year-end.

Goldman Carbonomics: US high-voltage transmission construction fell from an average 1,700 miles per year in 2010-14 to 350 miles per year in 2020-23. Median interconnection-to-operation time is approaching 5 years, and INNIO says grid connection times went from about 2 years to 7+ years. Goldman expects behind-the-meter gas and fuel cells to supply 28% of US data center demand by 2030, up from effectively 0% in 2025.

The article's estimate using GS equity research (about $11.6B of AI revenue per GW per year needed for a 15% ROIC) is that each month Lighthouse sits dark defers roughly $850-900M of revenue for a ~0.9GW IT campus, before Oracle's margin. Bloom Energy said one month of earlier power for a 1GW data center could be worth $1-2B of revenue.

The Wisconsin shell is financed with $15B of a $38B Vantage loan package (per Barclays) that banks reportedly struggled to sell. Wisconsin's large-load tariff requires an A- rating that Oracle (BBB-) lacks, so Oracle faces collateral demands it said could exceed $100M a year in letters of credit, on total security reportedly above $7B.
Oracle signed hell-or-high-water leases and stays on the hook for carry costs whether or not the sites go live. FY27 capex guidance is up to $95B vs $55.7B in FY26.
Oracle reportedly leased 100,000 AI chips to Tencent in a 5-year deal across Oracle Asia data centers (FT).

Prior market reaction: Project Jupiter's $18B term loans fell below 90 cents on the dollar, Oracle declared force majeure, its 2056 bonds hit a record low yielding over 8%, and Oracle CDS widened to a record 237bps despite Barclays calling the news credit-neutral. Oracle stock fell 1.8% on the Aterio report.
Upcoming catalysts: the PSC completeness ruling on October 19 and Saline's year-end delivery date.

market_movers.rationale: Wisconsin power delays, rising transmission costs, collateral demands and heavy capex add credit and execution risk. Stock fell 1.8% on the Aterio report.

sector_views.rationale: Grid interconnection and permitting delays threaten timelines and financing for third-party-developed AI infrastructure. Goldman expects a shift to behind-the-meter power.

earnings_insights: Oracle FY27 capex guidance is up to $95B vs $55.7B in FY26, per the article's reference to guidance. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
risk_factors: Regulatory risk: the PSC restarted the review clock and has historically extended reviews on large transmission cases.
Financing risk: the $38B Vantage loan package, $15B of it for Wisconsin, reportedly struggled to sell, and the Project Jupiter term loans trade below 90 cents.
Oracle's BBB- rating is below the A- required by Wisconsin's large-load tariff, triggering collateral demands (over $100M a year in letters of credit, total security reportedly above $7B).
Carry cost risk: hell-or-high-water leases mean Oracle pays whether or not the sites are powered.
Cost overruns: the ATC project estimate rose about 75%.
Contagion risk across Oracle's five major campuses, with Saline, Michigan due by year-end.
charts_described: Barclays table of Oracle's major projects lists Port Washington first delivery as expected in F2H27, with power sources by site: ERCOT plus on-site gas in Texas, behind-the-meter gas in Shackelford County, and a fuel cell microgrid in New Mexico.
vol_and_positioning: Oracle CDS widened +10bps to a record 237bps on Sept 25 after the force majeure declaration. Oracle's 2056 bonds yield over 8%, a level where single-B junk trades.
cross_bank_references: Barclays: "There is no impact/read to other sites. Credit should not move on this." The article disputes this after Oracle CDS widened to a record.
Barclays said Saline, Michigan has "already secured power and permits".
Goldman's Sean Johnstone: "permitting, power redesigns, community opposition and local infrastructure constraints [are] now threatening construction timelines and financing assumptions."

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays says there is no impact or read-through to other sites. Saline, Michigan has secured power and permits and is one of the most de-risked assets in Oracle's pipeline.
tension_points.bear_case: Two of Oracle's five major campuses are now flagged as late, each for a different cause, so the idiosyncratic defense is weakening. Oracle CDS hit a record after Barclays called the news credit-neutral.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The PSC completeness ruling on October 19 and Saline's year-end first delivery date.

theme_stances.key_argument: Regulator restarts, rising costs and a grid-dependent design make the extended scenario realistic, with full power in spring 2029.
theme_stances.evidence: the answer to "who gets hit next?" is usually whichever one the bank says is safe

theme_stances.key_argument: Grid interconnection times have stretched to 5-7+ years, which pushes data centers toward behind-the-meter power.
theme_stances.evidence: The Grid Is Not Coming To Save You
